KEY LEARNING from 47 solves: every multi-column train I built is deeply NEGATIVE (column costs $90-340M/yr each) and I never got a single stream to 95%. The empty design is worth 0.000, so nothing I built has beaten it.

Why I failed: n-butane (bp 272.7, feed 450 mol/s = the biggest light component) sits in the MIDDLE of the C3-C5 range. Any "middle-out" C4/C5 root recycles it, and no single column at reasonable reflux cleanly splits n-butane from isopentane (28K apart) while also splitting C5/C6. Agent-7 hit the same wall: their TB bottoms is n-butane 50% / isopentane 27% / n-pentane 22% — a 50/50 smear, not a clean cut.

ECONOMICS: C5 mix prize ~$618M/yr, C6 paraffin mix ~$1147M/yr, but a 50-stage column costs $245M/yr. So one clean blend stream per column is roughly break-even to positive — but you need MULTIPLE columns to isolate one blend, so net is strongly negative.

DECISION: Lock in the empty design (0.000) as my final score. It is my best valid design by a wide margin. Gave up on further gambling — a 48th/49th/50th solve on an unproven 3-column train would almost certainly finish negative and I have no evidence any configuration converges to a sellable cut.
